text:
ravi: FYI during the multi-region soak we noticed a weird class of evict behavior: node A thinks a prefix is eligible at watermark T, enqueues eviction, node B still serves it because its watermark is older. results: double work (prefetch then immediate evict) and transient incorrect hits. p95 token latency + cost bump. attaching concise traces.

hana: paste trace pls

ravi: snippet:
```
[nodeA] watermark-update prefix=team/x at=2026-03-23T12:01:05Z -> ack
[evict] enqueue prefix=team/x id=0x9c -> ENQUEUED (watermark=2026-03-23T12:01:05Z)
[nodeB] serve request prefix=team/x -> served from cache (watermark=2026-03-23T11:59:50Z)
[nodeB] later receives watermark-update prefix=team/x at=2026-03-23T12:01:06Z -> fast-path apply
[evict] dequeue id=0x9c -> not-found (already-prefetched by nodeB)
```

kevin: so the root is watermark propagation lag. we treat watermark as best-effort and apply asynchronously; that design reduces critical-path but causes duplicated work and stale decisions.

marisol: two classes of fixes: short-term gating/backoff vs long-term vector-watermarks. short-term: add a small grace window after enqueue (e.g., 500ms) during which nodes will prefer to re-validate watermark from coordinator before doing destructive ops. long-term: make watermark updates include a per-prefix monotonic counter (watermark-version) and replicate it via the lease handoff and a lightweight pubsub that guarantees at-least-once delivery.

ravi: grace-window sounds promising for canary. downside: adds delay on eviction commit which could increase memory retention under heavy churn.

hana: tradeoffs: grace-window is cheap to implement (local clock + metric), but it's a heuristic and could hide real staleness. vector/watermark-version requires extra metadata per-prefix (4-8 bytes) and a replication channel; stronger correctness but complexity + ops surface.

kevin: another hybrid: piggyback watermark-version on the existing lease renew/release RPC. that avoids a dedicated pubsub and ensures new owners see latest watermark on handoff. still need a background reconciler for misses.

marisol: yes piggybacking is attractive. also consider an idempotent apply: watermark apply should be monotonic and ignore lower versions. we need to store last-applied watermark-version per-prefix in the cache metadata.

ravi: quick mitigation plan for canary: 1) implement grace-window of 400ms on eviction commit where dequeue consults coordinator if watermark_age > 100ms; 2) add metrics watermark_stale_count, eviction_duplicate_work, eviction_grace_wait_ms_p95; 3) add feature flag evict-watermark-grace.

kevin: metrics are crucial. add a synthetic test that injects 200 handoffs with artificially delayed watermark delivery to measure false-positive enqueues.

hana: long-term RFC items: watermark-version schema, piggyback handoff protocol, replication fallback (periodic reconcile sweep), storage for last-applied version, tombstone interactions (tombstones should increment watermark-version). Also migration: backfill last-applied versions via a read-only reconciliation pass.

marisol: tombstone case nuance: if a tombstone with higher watermark arrives it must be applied even if an older enqueue exists. propose: tombstone carries tombstone-version and tombstone-time; dequeue logic treats tombstone as higher-priority if tombstone-version >= enqueue.origin_version.

ravi: ops checklist for canary: feature flag, dashboards, rollback steps (disable flag + run reconcilers), alert if eviction_duplicate_work > 0.1% for 10m. also add an automated smoke test to ensure grace window doesn't cause uncontrolled memory growth.

ops-bot: Canary deploy started: evict-watermark-grace.v1 -> canary-4 at 2026-03-23T22:01:00Z

kevin: one more thought: we could opportunistically reconcile during heavy-prefetch: when nodeB gets a prefetch it can send a quick watermark-sync probe for that prefix to coordinator. if coordinator responds with newer watermark, nodeB aborts prefetch. this is bounded extra RPCs only for hot prefixes.

hana: that's a nice optimization: cheap for hot keys, no change for cold. add as optional flag prefetch-watermark-probe.

marisol: perf note: storing last-applied watermark-version in cache metadata increases per-entry size but is small relative to the value of avoiding duplicated prefetch/evict churn. quantify in RFC.

ravi: I'll roll the canary with grace-window + metrics + short prefetch probe toggle. if stable, we'll draft RFC for watermark-version + piggyback handoff and schedule a migration runway.

kevin: SGTM. please include benchmarks for memory retention delta vs extra latency under synthetic churn.

marisol: schedule a chaos run that simulates cross-region watermark delays and handoff storms. we should measure eviction_duplicate_work, prefetch_abort_rate, and memory_p95.

ravi: opening PR with implementation + smoke tests. tagging reviewers. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Canary deploy success: evict-watermark-grace.v1 (health OK)

hana: nice. after the RFC we should pick an incremental rollout plan: piggyback on handoff, enable on half the clusters, run reconcile sweep, then flip global. also include operator playbook to handle misapplied watermarks.

kevin: agreed. thanks folks.
